name: Amrakhand
steps: Line a sieve with a clean fine cloth and set it over a deep bowl, leaving space for whey. Add yogurt, fold the cloth over it and refrigerate for 6 hours until thick and spreadable.
Transfer the drained yogurt to a bowl; expect roughly 450 g, depending on the original yogurt. Warm the measured milk and soak the saffron in it for 10 minutes.
Blend the mango flesh into a smooth puree without adding water. If the mango is fibrous, pass the puree through a fine sieve.
Whisk the thick yogurt and powdered sugar gently until smooth. Fold in mango puree, cardamom and all the saffron milk until uniformly golden and creamy; avoid vigorous beating.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to firm up. Divide among 4 bowls, scatter chopped pistachios on top and serve cold.
tips: Use a sweet, low-fibre mango and drain the yogurt in the refrigerator; excess whey makes the dessert runny.
passiveTime: Allow 6 hours to drain yogurt and at least 1 hour to chill after mixing.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
